sentences.text: 3 5. The petitioners herein have assailed the order dated 19.04.2023 passed by the Commissioner of Central Assam Division who is also the Arbitrator in terms with Section 3G of the National Highways Act, 1956.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 13 September, 2023.json

sentences.text:
The said order was passed in Case No.RR(CAD) 16/2023 on an application filed under Sub-Section (5) of Section 3G of the National Highways Act, 1956 by the private respondent No.10.
6.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 13 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: This Court has perused the said application which has been enclosed as Anenxure-1 to the writ petition.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 13 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: A perusal of the said application shows that the private respondents are aggrieved at the inadequacy of the compensation awarded by the competent authority, and as such, had filed the said application seeking enhancement of the compensation amount.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 13 September, 2023.json

sentences.text:
7. Taking into account that the reference made to the Arbitrator in question is only limited to the question of determination of the just and fair compensation on the basis of the well settled principles of law, the learned Arbitrator, in the opinion of this Court, ought not to have passed a direction to that effect that the respondents should not demolish the residential houses, structures and trees on the land covered by Dag Page No.# 5/6 Nos.49 and 51of Khiraj Myadi Patta Nos.15 and 9. More so, when by virtue of notification issued under Section 3D of the National Highways Act,
1956, the said property has already been vested upon the National Highway Authorities.
8.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 13 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: This Court further takes note of that in view of the said order dated 19.04.2023, the work to be carried out for four laning of the National Highway No.29 have been affected which hampers the public interest.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 13 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: 9. Taking into account the above, this Court, therefore stays the impugned order dated 19.04.2023 passed in Case No.RR(CAD) 16/2023 only to the extent wherein there is a direction upon the respondents not to demolish the residential houses, structures and tress on the land covered by Dag Nos.49 and 51of Khiraj Myadi Patta Nos.15 and 9 of the private respondent.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 13 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: 10. Another very relevant aspect of the matter arises for consideration for which the petitioners have been compelled to approach this Court is in view of a notification issued by the Principal Secretary to the Government of Assam, General Administration Department whereby the post of the Divisional Commissioner has been abolished and consequently there is no Arbitrator to adjudicate the case bearing No.RR(CAD) 16/2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 13 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: 11. Mr. B. Gogoi, the learned counsel appearing behalf of the respondent No.1 submits that there is a move on the part of the concerned respondent authorities to entrust an official from the revenue Department for the purpose of execising the power of the Arbitrator in terms with Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 13 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: Mr. B. Gogoi, the learned counsel on the next returnable date shall apprise this Page No.# 6/6 Court as to whether any official of Revenue Department has been entrusted to function as the Arbitrator in respect to those arbitration proceedings which arises out of the reference made under Section 3G (5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 13 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: 12. List accordingly.

sentences.text: Mr. G. Alom, learned counsel has appeared on behalf of the private respondents.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: The facts of this case, in a nutshell, is that the National Highway and Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd. (NHIDCL) has undertaken the work of widening/upgrading the existing National Highway No. 29 to a 4 (four) lane Highway.

entities.text: National Highway and Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: The Highway is passing through Karbi Anglong District of Assam.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: For the above purpose, plots of land belonging to the private respondents had been Page No.# 4/6 acquired.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text:
However, the respondents, being dissatisfied with the assessment of compensation made by the State PWD authorities pertaining to the valuation of the building and trees etc standing thereupon, had approached the Commissioner-cum-Arbitrator appointed under section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 for re-assessment of value of the building and Page No.# 1/6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28792080/
3 trees.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: The learned Arbitrator had passed order dated 19/04/2023 restraining the respondents from demolishing the residential houses/structures standing over the land and also from uprooting trees planted therein, by fixing the next date on 02/05/2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: On the next date i.e. 02/05/2023, the learned Commissioner-cum-Arbitrator had directed the Valuation Officer, Income Tax to assess the market value of the building/houses/structures of the petitioners at the rate applicable as on 31/11/2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text:
For assessing the plants/trees/crops attached to the land under acquisition, the District Commissioner, Karbi Anglong District, in association with the Divisional Forest Officer, Karbi Anglong East Division and the District Agriculture Officer, Karbi Anglong District, were directed to assess the names and numbers of the trees/plants/crops etc.
attached to the acquired plots of land of the respective petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: The matter was fixed again on 09/05/2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: However, by that date, the State Government had abolished the post of Commissioner-cum-Arbitrator appointed under section 3G(5) of the National Highway Act, 1956, as a result of which, the matter could not proceed any further.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: The interim order dated 19/04/2023 passed by the learned Arbitrator is still holding the field and due to the abolition of the post of Arbitrator, there is no possibility of that order being vacated/modified in the near future.
sentences._hearing_file: Page No.# 1-6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023.json

sentences.text:

However, the respondents, being dissatisfied with the assessment of compensation made by the State PWD authorities pertaining to the valuation of the building and trees etc standing thereupon, had approached the Commissioner-cum-Arbitrator appointed under section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 for re-assessment of value of the building and Page No.# 1/6 vs The State Of Assam And 9 Ors on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28792080/

The learned Arbitrator had passed order dated 19/04/2023 restraining the respondents from demolishing the residential houses/structures standing over the land and also from uprooting trees planted therein, by fixing the next date on 02/05/2023.
On the next date i.e. 02/05/2023, the learned Commissioner-cum-Arbitrator had directed the Valuation Officer, Income Tax to assess the market value of the building/houses/structures of the petitioners at the rate applicable as on 31/11/2022.
For assessing the plants/trees/crops attached to the land under acquisition, the District Commissioner, Karbi Anglong District, in association with the Divisional Forest Officer, Karbi Anglong East Division and the District Agriculture Officer, Karbi Anglong District, were directed to assess the names and numbers of the trees/plants/crops etc.
attached to the acquired plots of land of the respective petitioners.
However, by that date, the State Government had abolished the post of Commissioner-cum-Arbitrator appointed under section 3G(5) of the National Highway Act, 1956, as a result of which, the matter could not proceed any further.
The interim order dated 19/04/2023 passed by the learned Arbitrator is still holding the field and due to the abolition of the post of Arbitrator, there is no possibility of that order being vacated/modified in the near future.
Hence,
this writ petition.
The writ petitioners herein i.e. the Union of India as well as the NHIDCL, have primarily approached this Court seeking vacation/ modification of the interim order dated 19/04/2023 passed by the learned Arbitrator on the ground that due to the operation of the said order, the construction work of the National Highway has been stalled in that area.

Copy of this order be provided to the competent authority in the CPWD within two days, whereupon the CPWD authority shall appoint a suitable date for the valuation of the property within the next five days.
The valuation shall be carried out in terms of the order dated 02.05.2023, passed by the Arbitrator.
The appellants herein and the representative(s) of the NHIDCL may remain present and shall be permitted to append their signatory during the measurement as well as in the valuation proceedings.

Writ appeal stands disposed of in terms of the above observations and directions."

, it is submitted at the Bar that the same has already been carried out as per the order dated 02/05/2023 and valuation report has also been submitted.
